india.label: Diplomacy · 14 Nov
india.headline: Pakistan to send a minister to Delhi for SCO forum
india.summary: Pakistan said a minister would attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. Reuters described it as the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years.
india.context: A multilateral event gives officials a chance to share a room even when bilateral talks are limited. The forum is scheduled for 20–22 November.

india.label: Air quality · 14 Nov
india.headline: Delhi’s air remains very poor
india.summary: Delhi’s AQI was 348 at 9 a.m. on Saturday. Seven monitoring stations reported severe air quality.
india.context: The citywide reading can hide local differences. Check your nearest monitor if you need to make plans based on air quality.

india.label: Food prices · 14 Nov
india.headline: Tamil Nadu caps rice and pulse stocks
india.summary: Tamil Nadu imposed stock limits on rice, paddy and pulses as prices rose. Traders must declare inventory and bring excess stocks within the limits by 16 November.
india.context: Stock limits aim to release supplies into the market. Retail prices over the next few weeks will show whether supplies actually reach shoppers.

india.label: Mumbai · 15 Nov
india.headline: Mumbai’s CNG price rises to ₹91.50 per kg
india.summary: Mahanagar Gas raised the price of compressed natural gas in Mumbai and adjoining areas by ₹1.50 a kilogram, effective Sunday.
india.context: Fuel costs matter for CNG-dependent operators such as taxis and autorickshaws. Fuel-price changes and fare revisions occur on separate timetables.

india.label: Elections · 14 Nov
india.headline: A Pune voter-roll inquiry traces disputed address changes
india.summary: The Indian Express reported that Pune election officials flagged irregular requests to move voters between constituencies. The Maharashtra election office ordered an inquiry.
india.context: A voter’s address determines where their name appears on the roll. A disputed edit can leave someone looking for their name in the wrong constituency.

world.label: Ukraine · 14 Nov
world.headline: Zelenskyy questions a US proposal on European security
world.summary: Ukraine’s president said a European security framework floated by US officials could benefit Vladimir Putin. He said US officials had raised the prospect of a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO membership.
world.context: Territory and security guarantees are separate bargaining questions. Linking them affects what Ukraine would give up and what outside partners would commit to.

world.label: Climate · 15 Nov
world.headline: A fossil-fuel transition coalition presses ahead
world.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, a group of countries plans to present national transition plans after Colombia withdrew. Ireland and Tuvalu are set to take over leadership.
world.context: These national plans can show who is prepared to set implementation dates and commit funding, even while negotiations continue at the broader UN summit.

world.label: Shipping · 14 Nov
world.headline: Iran reports three tanker fires in the Strait of Hormuz
world.summary: Iran’s navy said three tankers were on fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters attributed the account to Iran’s navy.
world.context: Even disruptions to a few ships can affect this narrow route by raising freight and insurance costs and delaying deliveries.

world.label: Diplomacy · 14 Nov
world.headline: US and Russia push for a meeting China is wary of hosting
world.summary: Reuters reported that Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin were pushing for a meeting that Chinese President Xi Jinping was reluctant to host on the proposed terms.
world.context: Who hosts and who sits at the table can shape what gets discussed, especially when the talks involve other countries’ security.

world.label: South Sudan · 14 Nov
world.headline: South Sudan pushes its first national election to February
world.summary: South Sudan’s election commission moved polling day to 11 February 2027, replacing its previous December timetable.
world.context: Several delays have prolonged the country’s political transition. Voter registration and logistical deadlines will help show whether the revised date is workable.

markets.label: Indices · Friday close
markets.headline: Nifty and Sensex slipped into the weekend
markets.summary: At the 13 November close, Nifty 50 ended at 25,144.30 (−0.61%) and Sensex at 81,592.45 (−0.39%). Indian equity markets were closed over the weekend.
markets.context: Higher oil prices and inflation were among the factors Reuters cited. Compare the next opening move with market breadth to see how widely it is shared.

markets.label: Sectors and stocks · Friday close
markets.headline: Autos fell around 1% while Hitachi Energy India rallied
markets.summary: Nifty Auto slipped 1.07% on Friday, and metal and realty indices fell around 1%. Hitachi Energy India gained around 11% after quarterly results, according to Moneycontrol.
markets.context: Look at the earnings release for order intake and margins. A company-specific move can tell a different story from a broad sector index.

markets.label: IPO calendar · 15 Nov
markets.headline: Crystal Crop and Mahanadi Coalfields are on the IPO calendar
markets.summary: Crystal Crop’s offer was reported to open 18 November and close 20 November. Mahanadi Coalfields and SME issuer Watrana Rentals were reported to open 19 November.
markets.context: Check the exchange notice and prospectus for subscription windows, lots and listing dates. Crystal Crop’s reported 26 November listing date is tentative.

markets.label: Commodities · Friday quotes
markets.headline: Gold and crude give India two different price signals
markets.summary: On Friday morning, Financial Express cited Brent near $95 per barrel and an indicative India 24-carat gold rate of ₹1,36,330 per 10 grams. These were published snapshots.
markets.context: A weaker rupee can raise the Indian cost of both dollar-priced commodities. Check the city and purity for retail gold, and compare Brent with USD/INR.

markets.label: Foreign flows · Through 13 Nov
markets.headline: Foreign investors returned to Indian equities in November
markets.summary: Foreign portfolio investors put ₹84,290 crore into Indian equities in the first 13 days of November, the Times of India reported, following two months of net selling.
markets.context: Check whether fresh daily inflows continue as oil and inflation move. The month-to-date figure shows what has happened so far.

tech.label: AI agents · 14 Nov IST
tech.headline: ChatGPT Wallet gives agents a way to make purchases
tech.summary: The Verge reported that OpenAI’s ChatGPT Wallet lets its Dots agents make purchases on a user’s behalf after approval.
tech.context: Payments make the scope of approval important. A useful interface needs to show what the agent is buying and what the user is agreeing to pay.

tech.label: AI chips · Week ahead
tech.headline: Nvidia earnings will test expectations for AI chips
tech.summary: Reuters identified Nvidia’s upcoming results as a test for the AI trade after a volatile period for the chipmaker.
tech.context: Demand guidance can give a clearer signal about planned data-centre investment than a single day’s share-price move.

tech.label: AI labs · Week ahead
tech.headline: Anthropic prepares to face public-market scrutiny
tech.summary: Reuters reported that Anthropic’s planned IPO will be a major event for AI investors in the coming week.
tech.context: Public filings can give readers a closer look at how a frontier AI lab funds its computing costs and how quickly its revenue grows.

tech.label: AI governance · Context
tech.headline: Lawsuit asks court to halt frontier AI development
tech.summary: Reuters reported that a lawsuit against OpenAI, Google and Anthropic sought to stop frontier AI development. The companies were named as defendants.
tech.context: The complaint is a request for relief. Watch whether the court grants any temporary order and how it defines the work an order would cover.

tech.label: Creative tools · This week
tech.headline: Adobe previews a way for agents to edit native project files
tech.summary: Adobe announced a preview of local integrations that would let third-party agents work in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects via MCP.
tech.context: Editing the underlying project can let a creator inspect or revise individual layers and cuts after an agent has worked on them.

mind.label: Learning science
mind.headline: Remember more by trying to recall it first
mind.summary: In experiments using prose passages, Roediger and Karpicke found that recalling the material from memory improved delayed retention compared with spending the time studying it again.
mind.context: After a story, look away and say the main point in one sentence. Then check which detail you left out.

mind.label: Metacognition
mind.headline: You may understand the zipper less than you think
mind.summary: Rozenblit and Keil found that people lowered their ratings of how well they understood familiar mechanisms after trying to explain how those mechanisms worked.
mind.context: Before you say you understand a process, explain what happens at each step. The first step you cannot connect to the next is where to look closer.

mind.label: Social behaviour
mind.headline: When everyone thinks everyone else is fine with it
mind.summary: In a classic campus study, students thought their peers were more comfortable with campus drinking practices than they themselves were.
mind.context: A group can look united when many members privately have doubts. Asking people individually can reveal a different picture from watching the room.
mind.source: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

mind.label: Evolutionary biology
mind.headline: A jumping DNA sequence helped make moths darker
mind.summary: Researchers traced the dark form of the British peppered moth to an inserted piece of DNA in the cortex gene. Dark moths became common during industrialisation.
mind.context: This is a case where researchers identified a specific mutation behind a visible trait tracked through a changing environment.

mind.label: Natural selection
mind.headline: A drought shifted the beaks of Darwin’s finches
mind.summary: During drought on Daphne Major, medium ground finches with smaller beaks had a survival advantage when they competed with larger ground finches for seed.
mind.context: The advantage came from local conditions and a competitor. Evolution can favour different traits in a different place or year.

marketing.label: India · Brand film · 12 Nov
marketing.headline: SBI tells Diwali from the perspective of people on duty
marketing.summary: SBI’s Diwali film, made with Dora Digs, follows people who stay at work so others can celebrate at home. It pays tribute to essential workers whose shifts continue through the festival.
marketing.context: Look for the people who make a familiar occasion possible. Telling the story from their perspective can make a well-worn festive theme feel specific again.

marketing.label: India · Product storytelling · 12 Nov
marketing.headline: HDFC SKY gives each product feature a short film
marketing.summary: HDFC SKY announced eight shorts built around everyday money decisions. The first four use situations such as getting a raise or starting an internship to introduce investing features. TV, social cutdowns and regional-language versions extend the campaign.
marketing.context: Start a product demo with a moment the audience recognises. One situation per film makes it easier to picture when a feature would come in handy.

marketing.label: India · Public outreach · 1–30 Nov
marketing.headline: India pairs pension reminders with help to act on them
marketing.summary: The pensions department is promoting digital life certificates through SMS, radio, short films and local camps. Partners include banks, post offices and pensioner associations. Doorstep support is available where required.
marketing.context: Behavioural design can reduce the effort between hearing a message and acting on it. A reminder can tell people what to do, and nearby help can make the task easier to finish.

marketing.label: Global · Retail activation · 5 Nov
marketing.headline: LEGO lets shoppers step inside its holiday ad
marketing.summary: LEGO’s holiday film sends one brick through a fictional workshop set to Daft Punk. The campaign carries the workshop into physical stores with hands-on builds, minifigure activities and interactive window displays.
marketing.context: Give viewers a way to take part in the world you show on screen. LEGO connects the film to retail with an activity people can do as soon as they arrive.

marketing.label: Global · UK brand film · 3 Nov
marketing.headline: John Lewis turns gift anxiety into a Christmas story
marketing.summary: The UK retailer’s three-minute film follows a grandmother and a toy from her childhood as she searches for a gift her grandchildren will enjoy. It debuted across social channels and prime-time television.
marketing.context: The campaign starts with the pressure to get a gift right. A familiar worry gives the audience a reason to follow the story before the retailer enters the scene.
